1 · Membership Sale Commission

2 · Voucher Used - Service Commission
When a member redeems a voucher for a service, the performing provider earns 50% of retail × tier rate. The tier rate is 10% below the $10k monthly sales goal or 12% above. Full retail counts toward your $10k goal.
CategoryRetailBasis (50%)Below $10k (10%)Above $10k (12%)
Core Wellness$50.00$25.00$2.50$3.00

Core Wellness examples: Vitamin Shot · Cryotherapy · 3D Body Scan · EMS Mini · BrainTap
Premium Recovery examples: IV Drip · HBOT 60m · EMS Sculpting · Lymphatic Massage · Chemical Peel · Dermaplane
Worked Example - Carrie signs up a Premier member in June (below $10k goal)
Premier sale: $150 × 50% = $75.00
Core Wellness #1 (Vitamin Shot): $50 × 50% × 10% = $2.50
Core Wellness #2 (Cryotherapy): $50 × 50% × 10% = $2.50
Premium Recovery #1 (HBOT 60m): $185 × 50% × 10% = $9.25
June total for Carrie = $89.25
In July, if Viviana performs the redemptions, the service commissions go to Viviana - but the sale commission stays with Carrie (one-time, tied to sign-up).

📚 Peptide Basics
Provider reference: evidence-based fundamentals
🧬
What is a Peptide?
Mechanisms, structure & therapeutic action
▼
Clinical Definition
Peptides are short chains of 2–50 amino acids linked by peptide bonds. They occupy the pharmacologic space between small molecules (drugs) and full proteins - large enough to interact with complex biological receptors, small enough to be rapidly synthesized, modified, and eliminated by the body.
How They Work
Therapeutic peptides work by mimicking or amplifying natural biological signals. They bind to specific cell-surface receptors and trigger downstream signaling cascades - the same pathways used by the body's own hormones, growth factors, and cellular messengers. Because they mimic endogenous molecules, side-effect profiles are generally favorable.
vs. Proteins & Small Molecules
Proteins (50+ amino acids) like HGH are larger, longer-acting, and higher cost. Small molecules (drugs) act non-specifically and often suppress pathways. Peptides hit the middle - receptor-specific, short half-lives that preserve physiologic feedback loops, and endogenously cleared.
Pharmacokinetics by Route
💉
Subcutaneous
Most common. Slow absorption from SQ fat depot. Peak 15–60 min. Reliable bioavailability ~95%.
💊
Oral
Limited - most peptides degrade in GI tract. Exceptions: KPV (PepT1 transporter), BPC-157 (gastric acid stable), MK-677 (small molecule mimetic).
●
Intranasal
CNS-targeted delivery via olfactory route. Used for Semax, Selank, Oxytocin. Bypasses blood-brain barrier for brain-active peptides.
Why Peptides vs. Exogenous HGH?
Exogenous HGH suppresses the pituitary's natural GH production via negative feedback. Peptide secretagogues (Ipamorelin, Sermorelin, Tesamorelin) work upstream - stimulating the pituitary to produce GH in physiologic pulses. This preserves somatostatin feedback, prevents supraphysiologic spikes, and avoids axis suppression. The tradeoff: slower results, but significantly safer long-term profile and legal compounding status.
🔬
Can You Mix Peptides Together?
Compatibility, synergy & clinical combinations
▼
Short Answer: Yes - With the Right Combinations
Most therapeutic peptides can be combined safely and effectively. In fact, multi-peptide protocols consistently outperform single-peptide approaches when peptides are selected for complementary (non-overlapping) mechanisms. The goal is synergy - each peptide working on a different receptor or pathway to produce additive or multiplicative effects.
Evidence-Based Combinations
Ipamorelin + CJC-1295 (GHRP + GHRH)
The gold-standard GH stack. Ipamorelin stimulates GHS-R1a (frequency); CJC-1295 stimulates GHRH receptors (amplitude). Clinical data consistently shows greater total GH output than either peptide alone - two independent receptor systems converging on the same result.
BPC-157 + TB-500 (Wolverine Blend)
BPC-157 drives angiogenesis via VEGFR2-PI3K-Akt; TB-500 regulates actin polymerization for cell migration. Separate healing pathways produce significantly faster and more organized tissue repair than either peptide alone - preclinical and clinical evidence robust.
GHK-Cu + BPC-157 + TB-500 (Glow Stack)
Triple synergy: GHK-Cu adds collagen/elastin stimulation (MMP-2/9 remodeling + TGF-β synthesis) on top of the Wolverine healing mechanisms. Each works on structurally independent pathways - skin, tissue repair, and angiogenesis simultaneously.
⚠ Mixing Considerations
pH compatibility: Most peptides are stable in slightly acidic solution (pH 4–7). Brief mixing before injection is generally safe for common combinations.

New patients: Start one peptide at a time for 1–2 weeks before adding a second. Allows attribution of any side effects.

Avoid: Combining peptides with significantly different reconstitution pH, or those requiring different storage conditions (e.g., do not mix lyophilized peptides with saline-reconstituted peptides unless verified stable).
✅ Principles for Safe Combination
1. Different receptors: Pair peptides that act on different receptor types (e.g., GHRP + GHRH).

2. Complementary pathways: Angiogenic + structural repair (BPC-157 + TB-500).

3. No dose stacking: Don't combine two peptides with the same mechanism (e.g., two GHRPs).

4. Pre-mixed blends verified: Compounding pharmacy blends (Glow Stack, KLOW, Wolverine) use clinically validated ratios.
⚗
Is a Blend Less Efficient?
Pre-mixed vials vs. individual peptides - the science
▼
Short Answer: No - Blends Are Equal or More Effective
Pre-mixed peptide blends from licensed compounding pharmacies are not diluted versions of individual peptides. Each component is dosed at its therapeutically effective concentration within the blend vial. The common misconception is that combining peptides reduces each one's effectiveness - this misunderstands pharmacodynamics.
Dose Reality Check - Glow Stack Example
Component Glow 50 Blend Dose Typical Standalone Dose Verdict
GHK-Cu 30 mg 1–3 mg ✅ At or above standalone
BPC-157 10 mg 250–500 mcg ✅ Well above standalone
TB-500 10 mg 2–2.5 mg ✅ Well above standalone
Advantages of Pre-Mixed Blends
Verified stability: Compounding pharmacies test blended vials for chemical compatibility, pH stability, and shelf life.

Consistent ratios: Every injection delivers the same ratio of each peptide - no calculation errors.

Patient adherence: One injection instead of 2–3 dramatically improves protocol compliance.

Cost efficiency: Blended vials are typically more cost-effective than purchasing each peptide separately.
When Separate Injections Are Preferred
Titrating new patients: Start each peptide separately to identify any tolerability issues before combining.

Dose flexibility: If one component needs dose adjustment without changing the other.

Incompatible timing: Some peptides work best at different times of day (e.g., healing peptide AM + GH peptide bedtime).

Storage differences: If one peptide requires different storage conditions.
The Bottom Line for Providers
Pre-mixed blends are not a compromise - they are a clinically validated, pharmacologically sound delivery format. The key variable is always the dose of each component, not whether it arrives in a shared vial. When doses are therapeutically appropriate (as in licensed compounding preparations), blended vials produce outcomes equivalent to or better than separate injections, with higher adherence and lower injection burden.
